neighbours.label: ' on' or ' of' after plan, intend or make a point, before a verb in -ing (planning on picking up, made a point of not wearing), as opposed to 'plan to' and other uses of ' on'
fire: We were planning on visiting my parents in June.
The agency plans on launching two more satellites.
My brother fully intends on selling the house.
She made a point of greeting every guest.
Do you plan on staying for the whole concert?
The studio is planning on releasing a sequel.
I intend on finishing this book tonight.
He made a point of thanking the nurses.
quiet: We were planning to visit my parents in June.
The agency's plan to launch two satellites failed.
My brother fully intends to sell the house.
She had a point about the guest list.
Do you sit on the left at the concert?
The studio is located on a side street.
I put this book on the table tonight.
He was a big fan of the nurses.

notes: 'counting on getting' reached only 0.14 in a probe, so this is about plan-like verbs, not any verb + on.
